The '''Elias Bassalygo bound''' is a mathematical limit used in [[coding theory]] for [[error correction]] during [[data transmission]] or communications.<!--See "Hamming bound" for similar math-->

== Definition ==
Let <math>C</math> be a <math>q</math>-ary code of length <math>n</math>, i.e. a subset of <math>[q]^n</math>.<ref>Each <math>q</math>-ary block code of length <math>n</math> is a subset of the strings of <math>\mathcal{A}_q^n,</math> where the alphabet set <math>\mathcal{A}_q</math> has <math>q</math> elements.</ref> Let <math>R</math> be the ''rate'' of <math>C</math>, <math>\delta</math> the ''relative distance'' and 

:<math>B_q(y, \rho n) = \left \{ x \in [q]^n \ : \ \Delta(x, y) \leqslant  \rho n \right \}</math> 

be the ''[[Hamming ball]]'' of radius <math> \rho n </math> centered at <math>y</math>.  Let <math>\text{Vol}_q(y, \rho n) = |B_q(y, \rho n)| </math> be the ''volume'' of the Hamming ball of radius <math> \rho n </math>.  It is obvious that the volume of a Hamming Ball is translation-invariant, i.e. indifferent to <math>y.</math> In particular, <math> |B_q(y, \rho n)| =|B_q(0, \rho n)|.</math>

With large enough <math>n</math>, the ''rate'' <math>R</math> and the ''relative distance'' <math>\delta</math> satisfy the '''Elias-Bassalygo bound:''' 

:<math>R \leqslant 1 - H_q ( J_q(\delta))+o(1),</math>  

where

: <math> H_q(x)\equiv_\text{def} -x\log_q \left ({x \over {q-1}} \right)-(1-x)\log_q{(1-x)} </math>

is the ''q''-ary entropy function and 

: <math>J_q(\delta) \equiv_ \text{def} \left(1-{1\over q}\right)\left(1-\sqrt{1-{q \delta \over{q-1}}}\right) </math> 

is a function related with [[Johnson bound]].

== Proof ==
To prove the Elias–Bassalygo bound, start with the following Lemma:

:'''Lemma.''' For <math>C\subseteq  [q]^n </math> and <math> 0\leqslant  e\leqslant  n</math>, there exists a Hamming ball of radius <math>e</math> with at least 
::<math>\frac{|C|\text{Vol}_q(0,e)}{q^n}</math> 
:codewords in it.

:'''Proof of Lemma.''' Randomly pick a received word <math>y \in [q]^n</math> and let <math>B_q(y, 0)</math> be the Hamming ball centered at <math>y</math> with radius <math>e</math>. Since <math>y</math> is (uniform) randomly selected the expected size of overlapped region <math>|B_q(y,e) \cap C|</math> is 
::<math>\frac{|C|\text{Vol}_q(y,e)}{q^n}</math> 
:Since this is the expected value of the size, there must exist at least one <math>y</math> such that 
::<math>|B_q(y,e) \cap C| \geqslant {{|C|\text{Vol}_q(y,e)} \over {q^n}} = {{|C|\text{Vol}_q(0,e)} \over {q^n}},</math>
:otherwise the expectation must be smaller than this value.

Now we prove the Elias–Bassalygo bound. Define <math>e = n J_q(\delta)-1.</math> By Lemma, there exists a Hamming ball with <math>B</math> codewords such that:

:<math>B\geqslant { {|C|\text{Vol}(0,e)} \over {q^n}} </math>

By the [[Johnson bound]], we have <math>B\leqslant qdn</math>. Thus,  

: <math>| C | \leqslant qnd \cdot {{q^n} \over {\text{Vol}_q(0,e)}} \leqslant q^{n(1-H_q(J_q(\delta))+o(1))}</math>

The second inequality follows from lower bound on the volume of a Hamming ball:

:<math> \text{Vol}_q \left (0, \left  \lfloor \frac{d-1}{2} \right \rfloor \right ) \geqslant q^{H_q \left (\frac{\delta}{2} \right )n-o(n)}.</math>

Putting in <math>d=2e+1</math> and <math> \delta = \tfrac{d}{n}</math> gives the second inequality.

Therefore we have

: <math>R={\log_q{|C|} \over n} \leqslant 1-H_q(J_q(\delta))+o(1) </math>
